prompt:
`create_app(clock=...)` only half works. Orders and delivery estimates follow the
injected clock, but authentication still reads the wall clock directly (`time.time()` in
`shop/services/auth.py`). So in an app built with a frozen or fake clock, tokens from
`POST /auth/login` are stamped with the real time, and bearer tokens are checked against
the real time, which makes token expiry impossible to test and gives wrong results in
replay/simulation runs.

Please make the app's clock the single source of time for authentication: tokens issued
through the app (login) get `iat`/`exp` from the injected clock, and requests are
authenticated against the injected clock, so advancing a fake clock past
`TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES` makes authenticated requests fail with 401. The clock is a zero-arg
callable returning an aware UTC `datetime`, like `shop.utils.dates.utcnow`.
`issue_token`/`verify_token` must keep accepting an explicit `now=` (epoch seconds) for
direct callers, and `create_app()` without a clock must behave as before.
